title: 第23章 神农与大禹第24章 三仙火云洞求宝
content_zh:
更重要的是——
青蛟死了。
只要这条蛟不再拦河蓄水，不再借洪水走蛟化龙，那么下游的玄泽、长溪，乃至整片蜀地平原，都不会再受到威胁。
郑言在堤上站了许久，看着那具庞大的蛟尸，长长地吐出一口气。
“传令下去，蛟尸暂且不动，等蜀侯的人回来再做处置。伤员全部送回城内救治，阵亡将士的遗体收殓，登记造册。”
“是！”
“还有——”郑言顿了顿，看向被杨戬和祁虎抬着往后方走的祁澜。
“长溪世子祁澜，斩蛟首功，本将会如实上报蜀侯。”
常坤在旁边点了点头，没有异议。
他虽然是崇山伯的人，但方才那一幕他看得清清楚楚。
最后那两钺，确实是祁澜砍的。
蛟首，也确实是祁澜斩的，没他，在场的所有人都很有可能会死。
这功劳，整个灌江口的人都看在眼中，都得承他的情，谁也抢不走。
……
……
与此同时。
不知何处。
一片金黄色的麦田，在微风中轻轻摇曳。
麦穗饱满，颗粒分明，长势极好。
田边有一条清澈的小溪，溪水潺潺，鱼虾可见。

溪边坐着一个人。
穿着一身粗麻布衣，袖口挽到了小臂，露出结实有力的前臂。身材健硕，肩宽背阔，面容刚毅方正，下颌处留着短须，看上去约莫三四十岁的样子。
他手里握着一根竹竿，竿头系着麻线，线的另一端沉在溪水中。
钓鱼。
此人钓鱼的姿势很随意，竹竿都没怎么握紧，就那么松松垮垮地搭在膝盖上，人半靠着溪边的一块青石，闭着眼睛，像是在打盹。
但就在片刻之前，他睁开过一次眼。
那一瞬间，他的视线穿过了不知多少万里的距离，落在了灌江口的堤坝上，落在了那个举着石钺斩蛟的少年身上。
然后他又闭上了眼。
“感觉如何？”
一个苍老浑厚的声音从身后的麦田里传来。
说话的是一个老农。
身形佝偻，皮肤黝黑，满脸皱纹，穿着一件打了好几个补丁的短褐，脚上是一双沾满泥土的草鞋。
看上去就是一个再普通不过的种田老汉。
除了他的头上，长着一对粗壮的牛角。
老农从麦田里直起腰来，拍了拍手上的泥土，慢悠悠地走到溪边，在那个钓鱼的汉子旁边蹲了下来。
“怎么，看上那小子了？”
钓鱼的汉子睁开眼，嘴角微微一扯。
“谈不上看上。”
他的声音低沉平稳，带着一股子不紧不慢的劲儿。
“就是觉得有点意思。”

“哪里有意思了？”老农歪着头，牛角上沾着几根麦秆。
“他在堤坝上弄的那些东西。”钓鱼的汉子伸出手，比划了一下，“石笼填石，木排沉水，加固堤脚。这法子虽然粗糙，以前也没见过，但路子是对的，算是有几分巧思。”
“就这？”
content_en:
What's more important -
The green dragon is dead.
As long as this dragon no longer blocks the river to store water, and no longer uses the flood water to transform into a dragon, then the downstream Xuanze, Changxi, and even the entire Shu plain will no longer be threatened.
Zheng Yan stood on the embankment for a long time, looking at the huge dragon corpse, and let out a long breath.
"Second order, leave the corpses alone for the time being and wait for the people from the Marquis of Shu to come back before dealing with them. All the wounded will be sent back to the city for treatment, and the remains of the fallen soldiers will be collected and registered."
"Yes!"
"And -" Zheng Yan paused and looked at Qi Lan, who was being carried back by Yang Jian and Qi Hu.
"Changxi Crown Prince Qi Lan's meritorious service in beheading the dragon will be reported to the Marquis of Shu truthfully."
Chang Kun nodded beside him without any objection.
Although he was from Uncle Chongshan, he could see the scene clearly.
The last two axes were indeed chopped by Qi Lan.
The dragon's head was indeed beheaded by Qi Lan. Without him, everyone present would probably die.
This credit was seen by everyone in Guanjiangkou, and they all had to acknowledge him, and no one could take it away.
……
……
at the same time.
I don’t know where.
A golden wheat field swayed gently in the breeze.
The wheat ears are plump, with distinct grains and excellent growth.
There is a clear stream beside the field, with gurgling water and fish and shrimps visible.
There was a man sitting by the stream.
Wearing a burlap suit, the cuffs were rolled up to his forearms, revealing his strong forearms. He has a strong build, broad shoulders and broad back, a strong and square face, and a short beard on his chin. He looks about thirty or forty years old.
He was holding a bamboo pole in his hand, with a hemp thread tied to the end of the pole, and the other end of the thread was sunk in the stream.
fishing.
This man's fishing posture was very casual. He didn't even hold the bamboo pole tightly, it was just hanging loosely on his knees. He was leaning half against a bluestone by the stream, with his eyes closed, as if he was taking a nap.
But just a moment ago, he had opened his eyes once.
At that moment, his eyes traveled an unknown distance of thousands of miles and landed on the dam at the mouth of the Guanjiang River, and on the young man holding the stone ax to kill the dragon.
Then he closed his eyes again.
"How does it feel?"
An old and deep voice came from the wheat field behind him.
The speaker was an old farmer.
He has a stooped figure, dark skin, and wrinkles on his face. He wears a short brown jacket with several patches on it and a pair of muddy straw sandals on his feet.
He looks like an ordinary old farming man.
In addition to his head, there is a pair of thick horns.
The old farmer straightened up from the wheat field, patted the soil on his hands, walked slowly to the stream, and squatted down next to the fishing man.
"What, did you fall in love with that boy?"
The fishing man opened his eyes and twitched the corners of his mouth slightly.
"I can't say I'm interested in it."
His voice was low and steady, with a sense of unhurried energy.
"I just find it interesting."
"Where's the fun?" The old farmer tilted his head, with a few straws stuck to his horns.
"Those things he made on the embankment." The fishing man stretched out his hand and gestured, "Gabions were filled with rocks, wooden rafts were submerged in water, and the feet of the embankment were reinforced. Although this method is crude and I have never seen it before, it is the right way and it is somewhat ingenious."
"That's it?"
